**Root cause:** `app/lists.py` implemented `dedupe` as `list(set(items))`. Set construction discards insertion order (so `["a","a","b"]` came back as `["b","a"]`), and it raises `TypeError` for unhashable items like lists or dicts.

**Fix:** rewrote `dedupe` in **`app/lists.py`** (only file changed) to preserve first-occurrence order using a `set` for hashable items plus an equality-scan fallback for unhashable ones, with cross-group comparison so an unhashable value equal to an earlier hashable value is still deduped. It accepts any iterable (generators, tuples, views) and tolerates exotic `__eq__` implementations.
